title: Indonesia’s Mount Lewotobi Laki-Laki erupts, forcing airport to close
summary: A highly active volcano in eastern Indonesia erupted several times on Friday (Jun 5), spewing towering ash columns into the sky and forcing a local airport to close, authorities said.

title: Xi Jinping to meet Kim Jong Un in rare visit to North Korea
summary: China’s president Xi Jinping will meet Kim Jong Un next week in a trip to North Korea, in his first visit in nearly seven years, according to both countries’ state media.

title: Assistant Manager, security officer arrested over Horana bank robbery
summary: An Assistant Manager and a security officer have been arrested in connection with the robbery of Rs. 35 million from a state bank in Horana recently.

title: Zelensky proposes face-to-face talks in open letter to Putin
summary: Volodymyr Zelensky has called for a face-to-face meeting between himself and Vladimir Putin in a renewed bid to end the war.

title: Several injured in Boeing 787 nose-gear collapse in Frankfurt
summary: Several staff members were injured when the nose gear of a Boeing (BA.N) 787 jetliner unexpectedly collapsed ‌at a gate at Frankfurt airport on Thursday, its operator Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) said.

title: Immediate measures underway to address flooding on airport access roads
summary: Immediate action has been launched to address the recurring flooding of access roads leading to the Bandaranaike International Airport, following interventions by Deputy Minister Janitha Ruwan Kodituwakku.

title: Bear opens window in factory escape, Japanese police say
summary: A bear that was holed up inside an electronics factory in north-east Japan after attacking four people has eluded capture, apparently by opening a window by itself and fleeing under the cover of night, authorities said.

title: US plans to fight flesh-eating screwworm outbreak with flies and dogs
summary: US agriculture and health officials have outlined a plan to combat a flesh-eating parasite that has been detected in the US for the first time since 1966.

title: Several areas brace for 100 mm of rain
summary: Heavy rainfall of about 100 mm is expected at some places in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces and in the Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts today, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: ’World-first’ vaccine designed by artificial intelligence
summary: Artificial intelligence has been used to develop a ’’fundamentally new’’ type of vaccine that could protect against large swathes of viruses and prevent pandemics, say researchers.

title: Shakira to perform at World Cup opening ceremony
summary: Colombian pop star Shakira will perform her official song for the 2026 World Cup at the competition’s opening ceremony in Mexico.

title: Death toll rises to 13 in Anguruwatota elders’ home fire
summary: The death toll from the fire at the ‘Senehase Kedella’ elders’ home in Batagoda, Anguruwatota has risen to 13, after another victim succumbed to severe burn injuries while receiving treatment in hospital.

title: ’1990’’ under military rule: Suwa Seriya employees launch protest
summary: For the first time in its history, employees of the ’1990’ Suwa Seriya emergency ambulance service have launched a street protest yesterday in Colombo. Staff members gathered to voice their strong dissent against what they described as a newly imposed ’’military-style administration’’ and arbitrary workspace transfers that undermine the welfare of workers.

title: Water sources polluted with human waste, contained constituents unfit for human consumption
summary: Laboratory tests carried out by the health authorities have revealed that the spread of Meningitis in the Deniyaya area recently was due to the use of polluted water. It has been revealed that the people in the affected area depend on natural water resources including fountains and the community water supplies to meet their requirements of drinking water.

title: Construction sector on brink as 40% of firms become inactive - Sri Lanka Construction Association President
summary: About 40 percent of businesses in Sri Lanka’s construction sector have become inactive due to continued changes in tax policies, the increase in VAT and the depreciation of the rupee, President of Sri Lanka Construction Association Susantha Liyanaarachchi said.
